progressive_enhancement_surface_label: Example State official voter-information progressive-enhancement policy
delivery_role_note: Progressive-enhancement review keeps current voter-information pages answerable when richer client behavior degrades, but it does not replace content correctness, accessibility, or the current office/help lane as the authority source.
basic_technology_path_note: Critical voter-task pages are reviewed for a legible, actionable basic path that survives partial client failure rather than assuming full widget initialization.
crawlable_link_policy_note: The current office/help lane and other critical next-step routes remain exposed through ordinary HTML links even when richer client-side routing exists.
rendered_html_visibility_note: Major answer text should be present in basic HTML or reliable server-rendered output so the page does not depend on a fragile client waterfall to reveal the answer.
client_side_dependency_note: Richer widgets, client-side routing, and optional enhancements are reviewed as risk multipliers on critical page classes rather than as invisible implementation details.
third_party_widget_policy_note: Map embeds, translation helpers, analytics/tag-manager additions, and similar integrations may improve the experience but should not become the only route to a current answer or help lane.
browser_support_boundary_note: Declared browser-support scope may limit rich behavior, but the office aims to preserve a legible answer and recovery lane instead of a blank or spinner-only shell whenever reasonably possible.
degraded_client_recovery_note: When richer client behavior degrades, the office preserves a plain-language current answer and a stable office/help route rather than trapping the voter behind script-only controls.
